notes: lifeatspotify.com is Next.js over a headless WordPress; the jobs page fetches this wp-json 'animal/v1/job/search' endpoint once and paginates client-side ('Load more jobs'). The endpoint returns EVERY open job in one response — limit/per_page/page/offset params are ignored (verified: all return the identical full set).

Total oracle: __NEXT_DATA__ allFilters.categories positions sum to exactly the result count (90 at discovery); locations sum higher (120) because 29/90 jobs list multiple locations — never use locations as the completeness check.
id is a URL slug, not a numeric ID; detail URL is https://www.lifeatspotify.com/jobs/{id} (verified 200).
No posted/created date exists anywhere in the payload — first_seen_at in our DB is the only freshness signal for Spotify.
location maps to the FIRST of possibly several locations; full list lives in the raw 'locations' array. job_type is missing/false on some records (7/90 at discovery) and maps to None.

expected_min_jobs=30: one third of the discovery-time total (90). Spotify is a 7000+ employee public company; fewer than 30 open roles globally would be extraordinary and far more likely a truncated/filtered response, e.g. an accidental category filter ('c' param) which returns subsets.
